title: Composition and uniqueness of normalized adjunction formulas
statement:
Normalized comparison equations between ordinary and derived Hom bijections compose through two adjunctions. A right comparison isomorphism compatible with those equations identifies the canonical derived left-adjoint uniqueness map with localization of the ordinary uniqueness map. More generally the transpose of an inverse left-adjoint compositor followed by two successive adjuncts is the composite of the given arrows followed by the right compositor.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u₅ u₆ v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ v₅ v₆
variable {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {C : Type u₃}
  {DA : Type u₄} {DB : Type u₅} {DC : Type u₆}
  [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Category.{v₃} C]
  [Category.{v₄} DA] [Category.{v₅} DB] [Category.{v₆} DC]
  {F : A ⥤ B} {R : B ⥤ A} {G : B ⥤ C} {S : C ⥤ B}
  {FD : DA ⥤ DB} {RD : DB ⥤ DA} {GD : DB ⥤ DC} {SD : DC ⥤ DB}
  {QA : A ⥤ DA} {QB : B ⥤ DB} {QC : C ⥤ DC}
theorem normalizedAdjunction_uniqueness
    {H : A ⥤ B} {U : B ⥤ A} {HD : DA ⥤ DB} {UD : DB ⥤ DA}
    (a : F ⊣ R) (c : H ⊣ U) (ad : FD ⊣ RD) (cd : HD ⊣ UD)
    (εF : ∀ P, FD.obj (QA.obj P) ⟶ QB.obj (F.obj P))
    (εH : ∀ P, HD.obj (QA.obj P) ⟶ QB.obj (H.obj P))
    (ρF : ∀ K, QA.obj (R.obj K) ⟶ RD.obj (QB.obj K))
    (ρH : ∀ K, QA.obj (U.obj K) ⟶ UD.obj (QB.obj K))
    (hF : ∀ P K (f : F.obj P ⟶ K),
      ad.homEquiv _ _ (εF P ≫ QB.map f) = QA.map (a.homEquiv _ _ f) ≫ ρF K)
    (hH : ∀ P K (f : H.obj P ⟶ K),
      cd.homEquiv _ _ (εH P ≫ QB.map f) = QA.map (c.homEquiv _ _ f) ≫ ρH K)
    (η : R ≅ U) (δ : RD ≅ UD) (ν : ∀ P, F.obj P ⟶ H.obj P)
    (hν : ∀ P, a.homEquiv _ _ (ν P) ≫ η.hom.app (H.obj P) = c.unit.app P)
    (hρ : ∀ K, ρF K ≫ δ.hom.app (QB.obj K) = QA.map (η.hom.app K) ≫ ρH K)
    (P : A) :
    ((ad.ofNatIsoRight δ).leftAdjointUniq cd).hom.app (QA.obj P) ≫ εH P =
      εF P ≫ QB.map (ν P)
```

proof.text: Transpose successively through the two Hom equivalences. Naturality in the source moves the first left comparison outside the second transpose, and naturality in the target moves the second right comparison outside the first. For uniqueness, apply the transferred Hom equivalence to both candidate maps and use its unit normalization. Expand the composite Hom equivalence to obtain the general composite adjunct formula.
